questions.stem: Which agricultural practice is a major cause of eutrophication in rivers and lakes?

options.text: Excessive use of fertilisers containing nitrates and phosphates

questions.explanation: Excessive use of nitrate and phosphate fertilisers is a major cause of eutrophication. When it rains, these nutrients dissolve in water and run off into rivers and lakes, where they stimulate rapid algae growth. Careful application of fertilisers and buffer zones near waterways can help prevent this.

questions.stem: What is the difference between bioaccumulation and biodegradation?

options.text: Bioaccumulation is the build-up of pollutants in organisms, while biodegradation is the breakdown of substances by microorganisms
Bioaccumulation only affects plants, biodegradation only affects animals
Bioaccumulation is a natural process, biodegradation is artificial

questions.explanation: Bioaccumulation is the build-up of pollutants (such as heavy metals or pesticides) in an organism's body over time because they cannot be excreted efficiently. Biodegradation is the breakdown of substances by microorganisms into simpler, harmless products. Substances that bioaccumulate are often those that resist biodegradation.
